data: Diversity and Unity in Medieval Europe 500-1500 CE

Too often, especially in Europe itself, the European trajectory of history is taken to be not just a typical template, but one which somehow explains how this relatively small portion of the globe found a path to world domination. We miss too easily that that domination was really achieved by only three or four of Europe’s very numerous polities, not even all the largest ones, and that the continent remained and remains broken up and contentious in identity, even though it is often treated and even acts like a single politico-religious entity. This course looks at Europe’s first and formative millennium, and tries to distinguish what worked against its unity and maintained its distinct identities and practices, as well as the more usual opposite. Looking especially at religion and government, as well as the basic resources of life, it sets out to make clearer how Europe’s foundations mean it has never quite been one thing together, despite how much its components share.
